prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name a single universal “best” roofer for Denver (best choice depends on your exact needs and location), but I can help you find the right contractor and avoid common pitfalls after hail. A quick way to get started: tell me if this is a residential or commercial roof and your ZIP code and I’ll narrow options and give a short list of highly rated local contractors to contact. Meanwhile, below are concrete steps, what to ask, and red flags to watch for.

How to pick the right Denver roofer for hail damage
- Get at least 2–3 written estimates (more after a big storm surge). Compare scope, materials, warranties, and price.
- Prefer local or long-established regional companies (not out-of-state storm chasers).
- Look for manufacturer certifications (examples: GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster) — these let you get full manufacturer warranties.
- Ask about using Class 4 / impact-resistant shingles if you want extra hail protection.
- Check reviews (Google, Yelp), BBB rating, and ask for recent local references with hail repairs.
- Verify insurance and licensing:
  - Confirm they carry general liability and workers’ comp (ask for certificates).
  - Check business registration and any local contractor license requirements with Denver/Colorado authorities.
- Confirm they will pull required permits and handle municipal inspections.

Key questions to ask any roofer
- Are you licensed/registered to work in Denver? Can you provide proof?
- Do you carry general liability and workers’ comp? Can you show current COI?
- Are you certified by shingle manufacturers? Which ones?
- Can you provide at least 3 local references for recent hail repairs?
- What materials and brands do you recommend, and what warranties are included (labor and materials)?
- Will you handle permits and coordinate with my insurance company? Will you meet the adjuster on-site?
- Do you subcontract work? Who will be the day-to-day contact?
- What is your projected start and completion timeline? Do you provide a written contract?
- What are payment terms? (Avoid large upfront payments; hold final payment until permits are closed and lien waivers delivered.)

Insurance and claims tips
- Document damage immediately: clear photos and video of roof and other exterior damage.
- Notify your insurer promptly; follow their claims instructions.
- Get independent inspection and multiple estimates before signing anything the insurer offers.
- A reputable roofer can meet the adjuster and explain damage, but don’t let them fill out your claim forms for you.
- Beware of contractors who pressure you to sign an assignment-of-benefits without fully explaining it.

Red flags to avoid
- Door-to-door, pushy salespeople claiming they were in the area and can start immediately (storm chasers).
- No insurance certificates or reluctance to provide references.
- High-pressure upsells, demand for large upfront cash payments, or insisting you accept only contractor-arranged insurance settlements.
- Vague contracts, no timeline, or unclear warranty terms.

If you want, give your ZIP code and whether the job is residential or commercial. I’ll suggest a short list of next steps and what to ask each contractor when you contact them.
